items.method: Hold the dealer-positioning corridor (regime sign, flip, put and call walls, front expected move, signed net GEX and the gamma playbook) fixed against the benchmark's carried price, then track the change in the confirming internals versus the prior window — specifically the collapse of the cash-market breadth cushion from about 7 points to 0.5 point over the 60% participation line, the still call-heavy but firmer-put single-name premium, and the calm conditional-volatility regime — and test whether a persistent positive-gamma pin grinding into the call wall on a narrowing participation base is a genuinely new and less-supported configuration than the same pin the prior window, anchoring a direction-correct invalidation below the benchmark at the put-wall loss that would flip dealers back to amplifying a downside break.
items.note: The genuinely new configuration this window is not the dealer structure — which remains positive gamma with a pin-to-maxpain, patient, same-session-fade playbook — but the sharp thinning of the breadth that underpins it. SPY dealers read positive gamma with signed net GEX about +$4.51B, the flip at 768.59, the put wall 765 and the call wall 775 inside a tight plus-or-minus 2.61 front expected move on a 0.0911 ATM IV, and spot is carried at 772.79, above the flip and pressing toward the 775 call wall. The swing structure is cleanly Bull-stacked (20>50>200) with fast MA 769.21 over slow MA 711.63, the most recent auction is a Trend day up under Mixed control at VWAP 771.62, single-name option premium is still call-heavy at a 0.7159 call fraction (about $3.71B calls against about $1.47B puts, heaviest an NVDA 230 call at $55.7M on 6.9x open interest one day out), and the volatility model reads a calm 10.7464% regime. What changed is the internals: market-heatmap breadth has narrowed to 60.5% of 134 constituents, only 0.5 point above the 60% broad line, against a roughly 7-point cushion the prior window, and the option-flow put base has firmed from a sliver to about $1.47B. The constructive-pin lean therefore survives on price and dealer mechanics but on visibly thinner participation. The confirming trigger for the constructive case is spot holding above the 768.59 flip and grinding into the 775 call wall while breadth stays above 60%; the constructive-pin lean is invalidated on a daily close below ~765.00 on SPY, which loses the 765 put wall, drops spot beneath the flip into negative-gamma territory where dealer hedging would sell weakness, and would confirm the thinning breadth resolving to the downside.
items.title: The positive-gamma pin persists but its breadth cushion has collapsed: SPY dealers still hold positive gamma with the flip at 768.59 and walls 765/775 inside a plus-or-minus 2.61 expected move while spot is carried at 772.79 pressing the 775 call wall, yet market-heatmap breadth has thinned to just 60.5% of 134 constituents — barely a 0.5-point margin over the 60% line versus a 7-point cushion the prior window — so the mechanical grind into the highs is now riding a much narrower participation base

items.method: Cross-read the firming-on-price but thinning-underneath US internals (call-heavy single-name premium and a calm volatility regime against a breadth cushion that has collapsed to 0.5 point over the 60% participation line) against where leadership is actually being scored — the global-rotation composite ranking country ETFs versus ACWI and the real-assets 0-100 composite ranking crypto, broad-commodity, bitcoin, agriculture, oil, gold and silver vehicles — to test whether risk appetite still concentrates offshore and in real assets while the domestic tape merely confirms on a narrowing base, then, finding the leadership cluster resolves only to relative-strength scores and composite rankings rather than any price level on a committed-universe instrument, withhold the tactical call rather than publish one that resolves to unscoreable.
items.note: The second cross-model pattern this window is that the leadership scores continue to point offshore and into real assets even as the domestic tape stays firm on the surface but thins underneath, so the migration remains a where-is-the-bid observation rather than a confirmation of index direction. The US picture is still constructive on price — the benchmark is carried at 773.17 in a calm VIX 14.32 regime and single-name premium is call-heavy at a 0.7159 call fraction — but market-heatmap breadth has narrowed to 60.5% of 134 constituents, only 0.5 point above the 60% line. Against that, global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) first at 92.5/100 versus the US-heavy ACWI, with EWT (Taiwan) 76.3, EWC (Canada) 75, EWJ (Japan) 71.2, EWA (Australia) 70.2 and EWU (United Kingdom) 70 ahead of a middling US read across 13 markets scored. Real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities — ETH-USD 79.4, DBC 74.4 (six-month momentum +20.51%), PDBC 74.4 (+20.82%), bitcoin IBIT 73.1 and BTC-USD 70.8, agriculture DBA 72.2 — while oil (USO) 65.5 is a firm uptrend (+47.53% six-month) and gold (GLD) 39.3 is mixed and rate-shadowed with a -11.99% six-month pulse, silver (SLV) 19.4 weaker still at -18.47% six-month. Sector rotation echoes the risk tone domestically, rotating toward XLK as XLE rolls over. The pattern is coherent, and the newly thinning breadth makes the offshore-and-real-assets tilt more pointed, but it resolves entirely to relative-strength composite scores and country and vehicle rankings, none of which is a price level on a committed-universe instrument, so there is no direction-correct level at which the migration would be proven wrong. Rather than publish a tactical rotation call that could never be scored, the call is withheld; the observation stands as context that the marginal bid is concentrating offshore and in crypto and broad commodities while precious metals lag and US participation narrows.
items.title: Leadership is still being scored offshore and in real assets while US breadth barely holds the line: global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) at 92.5/100 far ahead of the US-heavy ACWI and the real-assets composite leads with crypto and broad commodities (ETH-USD 79.4, DBC/PDBC 74.4) as gold stays weak (39.3) and silver weaker (19.4) — a where-is-the-bid migration that now coincides with a thinning domestic cushion but still resolves only to relative-strength scores, so no scoreable tactical call is published
